requirement_text.REQ-066: Port src/api/errors.zig (272 lines) and src/api/response.zig (69) as Letflow.Api.Error and Letflow.Api.Response -- the single response/error contract every S4 route emits. Nothing in this batch renders a response body by hand once these exist. errors.zig is an RFC 9457 Problem Details builder. Port: the ProblemDetails shape (type as an absolute URI under a configured base, title, status, detail, plus the trace id field errors.zig carries with a "" default), the per-status constructors (problemNotFound and its siblings for 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 -- enumerate them from the Zig source rather than guessing which exist), and serialisation to a JSON body. Emit Content-Type: application/problem+json on error responses, per RFC 9457, and state in the moduledoc whether R-Co does the same or emits application/json (check response.zig's CONTENT_TYPE_JSON usage) -- if Letflow diverges, that divergence is deliberate and documented, not accidental. response.zig defines the canonical HandlerResult (status_code, body, content_type defaulting to JSON) and the typed success constructors that keep positive responses on correct status codes (200 vs 201 vs 202 vs 204). In Elixir the conn IS the result carrier, so port these as functions that take and return a conn (send_json/3, created/2, no_content/1, and the error counterparts) rather than transliterating a HandlerResult struct -- Zig returns a value because it has no conn. State that translation in the moduledoc. SECURITY (INV-4, INV-5): an error body must never carry secret material, a raw Ecto/Postgrex error, or a stack trace -- detail is a caller-safe string chosen by the handler, and an unexpected internal error maps to a generic 500 problem document whose detail does not vary with the underlying exception. Separately, the not-found problem document is the exact response a cross-tenant probe receives (REQ-072 enforces the routing; this requirement guarantees the two bodies are byte-identical by construction, because both go through one constructor).

result.summary: FAIL on routed item (1) only. The two new modules themselves are a clean, faithful, idiomatic port -- items (2), (3) and (4) all pass, no crutch, no supervision impact, no scope creep, no new warning or formatting failure. The gate fails because lib/letflow/router.ex:24-26 still hand-builds a 404 body, which is the exact thing REQ-066's own text forbids once these modules exist, and because send_problem/2 silently inverts errors.zig's trace_id precedence without documenting the divergence in a moduledoc that documents every other divergence carefully. Both rework items are mechanical and confined to files this run already touches. VERDICT (1) -- router.ex catch-all: VIOLATION, not acceptable scope discipline. `match _ do send_json(conn, 404, %{error: "not_found"}) end` is a hand-rendered error body sitting three lines above a module whose stated purpose is 'the single response contract every S4 route emits'. Delegating the private send_json/3 to Response.send_json/3 (which ELIXIR-DEV did do, correctly, per design §0.3) fixes the encode-and-send duplication but leaves the body SHAPE hand-rolled and off the Problem Details contract, so the system now ships two structurally different 404 documents. That is not a security defect today -- SECURITY-REVIEWER is right that a route-not-matched 404 exposes no tenant resource -- but it is the silent-drift class docs/anti-patterns.md's fragment-literal entry names, and that entry's own recorded precedent is that a real, low-risk, mechanical fix verified before requesting is FAIL/rework grounds rather than gold-plating. The design doc's silence on the catch-all is a gap, not a recorded decision, so requiring it overrides nothing. Scope is not expanded: router.ex is already modified by this run under design §0.3's own direction. REWORK 1a (ELIXIR-DEV): replace the catch-all body with Letflow.Api.Response.not_found(conn); if that leaves the private send_json/3 with only the /health call site, inline it or keep the delegation, either is fine. REWORK 1b (TEST-DESIGNER, Step 2e): test/letflow/router_test.exs asserts Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "not_found"} at lines 47, 59, 68 and 75. All four must move to the Problem Details shape. Their actual regression intent (REQ-046's removed routes 404 cleanly instead of raising UndefinedFunctionError and 500ing) is preserved -- the status assertion is what carries it. REWORK 2 (ELIXIR-DEV, lower severity, fix-or-document): Response.send_problem/2 does `%{problem | trace_id: conn.assigns[:trace_id] || ""}`, unconditionally overwriting the struct's trace_id. errors.zig's serialise/2 has the opposite precedence -- a non-empty p.trace_id WINS over the thread-local, and the doc comment states setting it explicitly is the supported override ('useful in tests'). Letflow therefore discards any caller-set trace_id, and blanks it to "" when assigns carries none. Nothing sets it yet so there is no live bug, but Error's moduledoc documents the content-type divergence, the dropped allocator fallback and the JSON-escaping fix as deliberate, and this divergence is undocumented -- which is exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md's 'don't silently re-decide' rule and the requirement's 'deliberate and documented, not accidental' clause are aimed at. Either restore source precedence (fall back to assigns only when problem.trace_id == "") or add a fourth translation note saying the inversion is intended. VERDICT (2) -- constructor split: CORRECT scope discipline, AGREE with CODE-DESIGNER and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR. Verified directly against R-Co/src/api/errors.zig: 19 pub constructors plus serialise. The 10 ported (bad_request/unauthorized/forbidden/not_found/conflict/unsupported_media_type/unprocessable/rate_limited/internal/service_unavailable) are exactly the status-generic set; the 9 deferred (problemPartitionMissingForWrite, problemUnresolvedCatalogRef, problemUnresolvedModuleRef, problemVariableSchemaViolation, problemUnresolvedPinOverride, problemUnknownPinRef, problemInstanceNotRebindable, problemEmptyPromotionPlan, problemInvalidPromotionSource) each encode a domain concept whose owning requirement has not landed. Porting them now would ship ten constructors with no caller -- abstraction ahead of the current requirement, i.e. the scope-creep class this gate exists to catch. Not an under-port: nothing an AC needs is missing. The port also correctly followed 'enumerate them from the Zig source rather than guessing', adding 415 unsupported_media_type and 503 service_unavailable beyond the requirement text's illustrative 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 list, because errors.zig has them. VERDICT (3) -- pattern-copy and Jason.Encoder: IDIOMATIC, no flag. The anti-patterns module-attribute entry does not apply to this shape. That entry is about ONE identical literal repeated at two call sites, where an edit to one and not the other silently drifts. Here nothing is repeated: each constructor's slug, title and status are all distinct, so there is no shared source of truth to drift. The literals that ARE shared are already hoisted correctly -- @problems_base for the base URI (matching errors.zig's `const BASE`), @internal_error_detail and @not_found_detail for the two INV-4/INV-5 fixed strings. A shared private builder(slug, title, status, detail) would save roughly four lines per constructor while costing the per-status @doc/@spec surface and the 1:1 line-up with errors.zig that makes this port cheap to diff against its source during migration. Pattern-copy is the right call. @derive {Jason.Encoder, only: [:type, :title, :status, :detail, :trace_id]} is also correct and is the better of the two options: the explicit only: list pins field order to errors.zig's serialise format string (verified byte-order match: type, title, status, detail, trace_id), and it structurally prevents a future added struct field from silently appearing in an error body -- an INV-4-adjacent benefit Map.from_struct/1 would not give. Using Jason rather than raw interpolation also fixes a genuine unescaped-string bug in the Zig source (allocPrint with literal "{s}" does not escape quotes/backslashes/control chars in detail), which the moduledoc correctly records as a fix that must not be reverted. VERDICT (4) -- decision 0001 consistency: CONFIRMED, no Phoenix. mix.exs carries plug ~> 1.15, bandit ~> 1.5, jason ~> 1.4 and no phoenix dependency; grep for Phoenix across lib/letflow/api/ and router.ex hits only router.ex's own moduledoc line asserting 'Plug + Bandit, no Phoenix'. No Phoenix-shaped idiom smuggled in either: no use SomethingController, no render/3 or view/template layer, no action_fallback, no Phoenix.Controller.json/2. Response is explicitly not a Plug (no @behaviour Plug, no init/1 or call/2) and says so in its moduledoc; both modules are plain function libraries over Plug.Conn. Error has no Plug dependency at all. Consistent with 0001 as reaffirmed by REQ-065. WARNINGS AND FORMATTING (no re-litigation of ISS-0106): `mix format --check-formatted` scoped to lib/letflow/api/error.ex, lib/letflow/api/response.ex and lib/letflow/router.ex exits 0 -- this run's files are clean. `mix compile --force` filtered to those three paths produces zero warnings; the warnings that do appear (e.g. lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:881) are pre-existing on main and are ISS-0106/GH#354's toolchain-pin problem, not this run's. No new warning and no new formatting failure attributable to this run. OTHER GATE QUESTIONS: gen_statem/crutch -- N/A, no state machine in either module, and no GenServer-with-case-state anywhere in the diff. Supervision -- untouched: no process, no spawn, no GenServer, no supervisor child added; both modules are pure functions and conn-threading functions, so per-instance isolation via Letflow.InstanceSupervisor is unaffected. Type safety -- no gap worth filing: status is typed 400..599 on the struct, and the public API makes an inconsistent type/title/status triple unreachable because every triple is fixed inside one constructor. No docs/issues/ entry filed. NON-BLOCKING NOTES (recorded, not dropped, no action required this run): (a) @problems_base uses Application.compile_env/3, so the base URI is baked at compile time and a runtime config change needs a recompile. This is correct usage -- compile_env registers the recompile check -- and matches errors.zig's `const BASE`; noted only so a later requirement that wants per-tenant problem URIs knows it must move to runtime config deliberately. (b) lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex's reject_migrating/1 still builds and sends its own response inline; design §3 correctly marks simplifying it onto Response.service_unavailable/2 as optional and out of scope here. Worth picking up in REQ-070/REQ-071 when the pipeline is assembled -- flagged as the second place in this codebase reaching around the shared response contract, which is the trend to watch now that the contract exists. (c) The catch-all exception 500 plug (Plug.ErrorHandler in the router) remains correctly out of scope per design §0.3; internal_error/1 is safe to call, nothing yet calls it automatically. RE-REVIEW SCOPE: on resubmission I need to re-check only router.ex's catch-all, the router_test.exs assertions, and send_problem/2's trace_id handling. Everything else in this diff is signed off as-is.
